newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India yaws in placid end to week.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India yaws in placid end to week.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) ended little changed as a speech from Finance Minister P. Chidambaram failed to deliver many substantial changes to corporate tax.
"The moves were very cosmetic, the only result of the bank loans will be to allow traders to hold on and sell at a higher price," said a trader.

Chidabaram told parliament investments in mutual funds will be exempt from capital gains tax and allowed foreign funds to run debt funds as well as raising the ceiling on bank loans against shares and played with dividend and interest income taxes.
Announcements on changes to minimum corporate taxes are expected next week.

The James Capel Indian GDR Index fell 0.28 points, or 0.39 percent to 73.55 points, a premium of 13.02 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index ended 8.83 points lower at 3,508.07.

"The market will open up next week, partly because clients globally have been sway all this week, but the rally may only last three days. It is starting to get difficult to see this market recovering," the trader said.
Traders said that GDRs such as Bajaj Auto, which had not taken part in the recent market fall looked vulnerable.
"It only takes one big seller to come in and all those people who want the stock are sated," said one.
Bajaj GDRs closed down 19 cents at $36.75/$38.25.

The Capel Taiwan Index fell 1.24 points, 1.37 percent to 88.77 points a premium of 3.34 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index ended down 14.73 points or 0.23 percent at 6,290.23.
Asian equities were hit by renewed talk that semiconductor prices were sliding again.
The Capel Korea Index fell 3.1 points 4.52 percent to 65.54 points, a premium of 21.82 percent over the local market after the the Korea Composite Index ended 2.77 points lower at 784.37.
Samsung Electronics global depositary share fell $2.38 to $19.00/$20.00 after the local fell 3,600 won to its daily trading limit of 56,700 won.
Traders said that the spot price for 16-megabit DRAMs had fallen to $9.00 from $12 a unit in August and $50.10 a year ago.
